claims.text: The baseline as-deposited FeNiCrCoCu coating is chemically homogeneous and single-phase, without induced elemental segregation.
The controlled intervention is annealing the coating in argon at approximately 800°C for 1 hour.
Annealing at approximately 800°C for 1 hour will promote moderate Cu segregation to grain boundaries in the FeNiCrCoCu coating.
The annealing-induced Cu segregation will form evenly distributed Cu-rich layers or precipitates at grain boundaries.
Cu-rich grain-boundary phases inhibit dislocation transmission.
Cu-rich grain-boundary phases act as a lubricious barrier during sliding.
Dislocation behavior governs high-temperature microscopic deformation and mechanical response.
Impeded dislocation motion caused by Cu-rich grain-boundary phases limits localized plastic deformation during sliding.
Limiting localized plastic deformation enhances the coating's overall wear resistance.
Relative to the as-deposited baseline, the annealed Cu-segregated coating will have a lower wear rate during sliding at 500–700°C.
Relative to the as-deposited baseline, the annealed Cu-segregated coating will exhibit less microscopic plastic deformation during sliding at 500–700°C.
The predicted benefit applies only while Cu segregation remains controlled and does not cause detrimental coarsening or deleterious phases.
Excessive Cu segregation could reduce coating cohesion.
